note.p: Thomas Holcroft was one of Godwin's closest friends for many years. He was a sigificant collaborator in Godwin's writings, notably Political Justice as well as being an important dramatist and novelist in his own right. Holcroft left for Germany in 1799, partly due to the notoriety he had gained as an 'acquitted felon' of the 1794 Treason Trials. He returned to England in 1802 and had further success on the stage. Godwin and he fell out over a character in Godwin's Fleetwood which Holcroft felt was based on him. They were reconciled on Holcroft's deathbed.

Godwin’s first mention of Holcroft is in 1788, which is used consistently until the first instance of abbreviation of ‘Ht’ in 1792. Other variations have included ‘H’ (where context has determined that the initial refers to Holcroft) and Holct. 1795 is the last mention of Holcroft’s full name, and thereafter Godwin uses Ht consistently. Where possible, when Godwin refers to Holcrofts plural, we have established his partner based on chronology, as he married several times. Holcroft married in 1765 and has a daughter Ann. His wife died prematurely but no further details are known. In 1774 he married Matilda Tipler, wiith whom he had his son William and daughter Sophy, this wife dying c 1775. He married his third wife, Dinah Robinson, in 1778, with whom he had a daughter Fanny. The diary notes the separation of Holcroft from his third wife on 6 January 1790, and notes her death on 31 October 1790. Godwin seems to have had no independent relationship with Holcroft's third wife (hence, left uncoded). He married his fourth wife, Louisa Mercier on 4 March 1799. The DNB makes no mention of issue from Hocroft's fourth marriage, but Godwin refers to L Ht and sons in the diary from 1803. Also, the account of Holcroft's death in his Life refers to an incident where Holcroft asks his wife if it is her children making a noise on the stair (p. 310). The Morning Chronicle (25 March 1809) reporting Holcroft's death refers to him having left an amiable wife and six children under the age of nine (all baptised together at St Marylebone on 1 March 1809) and two daughters from a previous marriage! His widow married the playwright *James Kenney* in 1812.>

There is a reference to a 'Ht' on 4 Jan 1802 which has been left uncoded as Holcroft is still abroad. '2 Hts' and '3 Holcrofts' entries which appear 1802-5 have been coded for Thomas and Louisa. After Holcroft marries Louisa, all instances of 'Hts' have been coded for her as well. Similarly to other entries, she has also been included in any meals Godwin takes at 'Ht's' and for 'Call on Hts' but NOT for any 'call on Ht' or 'Call at Ht's'. N.B. This is despite evidence of Godwin's inconsistent use of the possessive apostrophe ie 'Dine with Nicholsons, Smiths, Ht's, etc' Note also on 9 Aug 1804, Godwin refers to 'L and T Ht' this has been coded as Thomas and Louisa, despite the unusual nature of the reference.

There are also a number of occasions when Godwin uses H to refer to Holcroft - many of these are clear, althopugh the occasions in 1801 and 1802 are suspect - since, although Holcroft may have made fleeting returns to the UK during the peace of Amiens, we have no corroboration. The H's in 1808 clearly refer to Hodgkins, Godwin's errant shopman. We have not coded the Hs for 1812, 1819, 1820, 1823, and 1825unless we have the right contextual data, and it is likely that these are oftn to be identified from those with whom they appear. Nothing suggests they are references to a single person.

There is a range of references to Holcroft's activities that can be traced through the entries, although the meaning of many of them remains obscure. For example, 17 September 1788 'Explain to Holcroft' and 29 September 1788 'Holcroft explains to Robinson'. In November 1789 a series of entries from 8 November 1789 to 17 November 1789 provides a narrative of the running away of Holcroft's son, their pursuit to Gravesend and then Deal; the suicide of his son, and then his funeral. This is followed in 6 January 1790 by 'Separation of H and sa femme' . Holcroft's third wife (Diana Robinson) dies on 31 October 1790 and an inquest and funeral follow on 2-3 November 1790. Unsurprisingly, Holcroft also features largely in references to quarrels or 'demêlé'.

Ed Pope has suggested corrections which we have incorporated. He also has the following more 'narrative' notes: The entries from 1805 and 1806 below show Holcroft and Godwin falling out over what Holcroft considered a character based on him in Godwin's novel Fleetwood. Ht was Godwin's abbreviation for Thomas Holcroft. Note the use of brackets when Godwin accidentally saw Holcroft. Godwin also used brackets when he saw famous people at the theatre. I take them to mean "saw but didn't speak". 15.2.1805 sup at Ht's, w. Mercier. Fleetwood published / 28.2.1805 note from Ht : call on Nicholson (not seen) : send to Kentish Town : Lamb calls / 3.3.1805 write to Ht : call on Nicholson / 4.3.1805 write to Nicholson on Ht / 12.3.1805 again / 14.10.1805 (meet Ht) / 23.10.1805 again / 23.11.1805 theatre, adv. (Ht) and mrs Foulkes / 18.4.1806 call on Lamb (adv. Ht) There were no further mentions of Holcroft until a few days before his death, when Holcroft's sister-in-law Elizabeth Mercier called on Godwin who went straight to see Holcroft. Godwin then called each day but only got to see Holcroft one more time. George Tuthill was a doctor as well as a good friend of Holcroft's. William Hazlitt and Henry Crabb Robinson were calling on Godwin, perhaps for news of Holcroft. Hazlitt was a regular caller on Godwin at the time but Robinson not. 19.3.1809 E Mercier calls : call on Ht; adv. Tuthil / 20.3.1809 call on Ht (not seen) (adv. Harwood, Thelwal and Dawe) / 21.3.1809 call on Ht; adv. Harwoods : Hazlit calls and H Robinson (not seen) / 22.3.1809 Hazlit calls : call on Ht (not seen) / 23.3.1809 Hazlit, H Robinson and Dawe call : call on L(ouisa) Ht; adv. Harwoods, mrs Nicholson and Lambs. Ht dies The days after Holcroft's death were full of collective grieving. Clipstone Street was where Holcroft's house was. Godwin took tea with William Nicholson, William Harwood and George Tuthill several days running. Sarah Nicholson, Mary Lamb, Margaret Dawe and Mary Jane Godwin rallied round the widowed Louisa Holcroft. It looks like a collection taken at the funeral came to £83 and was entrusted to Sharon Turner DNB 1768-1847. Godwin called on Thomas Hardy DNB 1752-1832 probably to help arrange a memorial meeting for Holcroft at the Crown and Anchor, and ended up seeing more of John Thelwall than he had for years. W N and G T at the Crown and Anchor were Nicholson and Tuthill. Ralph may have been the artist George Keith Ralph DNB 1752-1811+. Godwin had first called on him on 18.2.1809 so probably not in connection with Holcroft, but he attended both the funeral and the Crown ans Anchor, so may have been a friend or admirer of Holcroft. 24.3.1809 Ralph calls : tea L Ht's, w. M J / 26.3.1809 call on L Ht; adv. mrs Nicholson, M(ary) Lamb and Tuthil : H Robinson au soir / 27.3.1809 tea Nicholson's, adv. Harwood : Clipstone Street, for M J; adv. M(argaret) Dawe / 28.3.1809 tea Nicholson's, w. Harwood; adv. Tuthill / 29.03.1809 tea Nicholson's, w. Harwood and Tuthil : Clipstone Street, for M J; adv. M Dawe / 1.4.1809 Funeral of Ht, w. Shield, Nicholson, Harwood, Buchan, Lamb, Thelwal, Dawe and Ralph : Sh.Turner's, w. Harwood, Thelwal and £83. R Cloud sups; adv. C Mercier / 2.4.1809 Call on Hardy : tea Nicholson's, w. Harwood and Tuthil; adv. L and F(anny) Ht / 3.4.1809 Nicholson calls : call on Nicholson, w. M J : sup at L Ht's, w. M J; adv. E M(ercie)r / 4.4.1809 tea Nicholson's / 5.4.1809 Crown and Anchor; present, W N, G T, Thelwal, H Robinson, Lamb, Stodart, Collier, Le Maitre, Hardy, Ralph, Spyring and Dawe : dine at Thelwal's / 6.4.1809 tea, adv. H Robinson: tea Nicholson's. Hardy calls / 9.4.1809 Mrs Ht and V Ht breakfast; adv. Dawe / 10.4.1809 Nicholson calls / 11.4.1809 call on Lambs; adv. L Ht : Nicholson calls / 13.4.1809 meet Nicholson, at L Ht's : dine at Thelwal's, w. Nicholson, Wolcot, Mortimer, Soane, Brittons and miss Pate
The diary also refers to Harwood Holcroft, probably one of his sons, named in gratitude after Col. Harwood who was a close friend to Holcroft as well as being his son-in-law (with Ann).
